topics.topic: Cycle-detection graph scope (which nodes/edges count, including synthetic endpoints and guarded edges)
questions: Does cycle detection include synthetic flow endpoints (empty-node flow input/output endpoints) or only real flow nodes?
When checking acyclicity, are guarded edges always included as graph edges, or only edges that can deliver under some guard valuation considered?

judgement.divergence: One implementer treats phase-7 acyclicity as over all declared directed edges (guarded edges included) and refuses any flow version containing such a cycle; another excludes some guarded edges (for example unless they can deliver) and accepts some of those versions. The agent notices at compose/prove/activate because one kernel returns a proof failure and the other returns proven.
judgement.why: The rules define acyclicity but do not state whether guarded edges are always part of the cycle graph.

topics.topic: Operation path placeholder grammar and whether repeated placeholder names are valid
questions: What is the exact placeholder grammar and validation (unmatched braces, empty name, repeated placeholders, escaping literal braces)?
If the same placeholder name appears multiple times in the path, is that valid (same input substituted in each occurrence), or should such a binding be refused as ambiguous?

judgement.divergence: One implementer enforces a strict placeholder grammar (and may refuse unmatched/empty/repeated placeholders at proposal time); another accepts repeated placeholders and/or treats malformed braces as literals, so the binding is accepted and requests are sent with different concrete paths. The agent notices at binding proposal/acceptance, and the external service notices different request URLs.
judgement.why: The text says how `{name}` placeholders map to inputs but does not fully close the placeholder grammar and repeated-name validity.

topics.topic: Approved preview format/order for `many` file inputs
questions: For a `many` file input, what exact preview structure/order is shown and therefore approved (single aggregate item vs per-element list in order)?

topics.topic: Definition of file media-type equality for proof comparison
questions: Is media-type equality byte-for-byte string equality, or MIME-normalized equality (case-insensitive type/subtype, parameter handling rules)?

topics.topic: Execution-class assignment for records with neither inputs nor outputs
questions: What class is assigned when an execution record names no inputs and no outputs (for example `skipped_by_guard` / `upstream_failed` records without payload)?

topics.topic: Filesystem access boundary for function implementations vs declared file ports
questions: Are function implementations allowed to read/write arbitrary files inside the exchange directory, or should filesystem access be limited strictly to declared file-port inputs/outputs only?

topics.topic: How size limits apply to `many` value ports (whole array vs per element)
questions: For a `many` value, is the size limit applied to the whole array encoding, to each element, or both?

topics.topic: Post-send persistence failure policy after an effectful HTTP attempt
questions: If the HTTP attempt has already been sent (or answered) but the outcome store call fails, what must the kernel do to preserve run/effect truth: stop the process, return refusal, or continue with an implicit recovery path?

topics.topic: WaitingPoint lifecycle when an element’s waiting reason changes
questions: For one element transitioning from `outcome_unknown` to `owner_approval`, does the kernel replace the existing waiting point or keep multiple waiting points for that element over time?

topics.topic: Whether TrialCase.expected_outputs must be complete or may be a subset
questions: When expected_outputs is present, must it name all output ports exactly, or may it name only a subset to assert partial expectations?

topics.topic: Whether pre-send effectful-check failures must still create owner-approval stops
questions: If an effectful node fails a pre-send check (for example `binding_stale` or missing instance), must it still stop and create an approval request first, or fail immediately without any approval record?
